thread:
incident-bot: PAGING — Dedicated tenant 'lyra-enterprise' pool at 98% GPU utilization, queueing increasing. Severity: P1. Routing on-call: @mike. Auto-escalation in 5m if no ack.
mike: oncall mike here, ack. joining.
lyra-support: Lyra SRE here — customer reports steady 504s and long tail latencies for chat endpoints starting ~09:12 UTC, error rate ~14%. Key customers impacted (lyra-prod).
jia: looking at metrics — GPU queue length hit 400, avg token latency spiked to 1.8s/token. Autoscaler didn't add new nodes; pool is pinned to dedicated capacity (no spare GPUs).
elaine: confirmed — pool's min/max set to fixed capacity per contract. Burst to shared capacity is possible if we enable emergency spill but requires approval.
sara: @mike what are options? We can't evict since it's single-tenant dedicated. Could we fall back to a lighter model or quantized variant for some routes?
mike: quick triage: 1) ask lyra to pause bulk jobs/rate-limit heavy clients 2) enable emergency spill to preemptible burst (30m) 3) switch heavy routes to quantized model variant (gpt-small-q4) 4) if none feasible -> open handoff to infra for manual capacity resize. Which we can do fastest?
lyra-support: We can ask customer to throttle non-interactive jobs immediately. We also have a quantized variant (v2-q4) but it hasn't been promoted for prod. Can enable if you accept potential quality regression.
jia: I'll prepare a quick canary of v2-q4 on 10% traffic. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout create --tenant lyra-enterprise --model v2-q4 --route /chat --percent 10
```
Expect lower GPU memory and ~2.2x throughput.
elaine: I'll kick off emergency spill approval. Need product or ops lead consent for billing/contract exception. @sara can you confirm billing contact?
sara: Billing is SCC billing alias; I pinged them. Also pinging @mike for legal/contract waiver if we exceed reserved capacity.
mike: I approve emergency spill for 30m as temporary mitigation. Elaine, proceed. @jia run the canary for v2-q4 and monitor error rate.
ops-note: enabling spill -> allocating preemptible GPUs from shared pool. Risk: noisy neighbor, no SLA.
(2m later) jia: Canary rolling — 10% traffic switched. Early results: error rate on canary down 40%, latency -20%. Good signal.
lyra-support: Customer applied a soft throttle to background indexing jobs; traffic dropped ~18%. Combined with canary we're seeing queue length reduce.
elaine: Spill approved and enabled for 30m. Command executed: 
```
redwoodctl capacity spill --tenant lyra-enterprise --duration 30m --reason "emergency saturation"
```
mike: monitoring. If we see sustained >85% after 30m, we'll escalate to capacity resize (procurement + infra) — that will take hours.
jia: current metrics (summary): GPU util 72%, queue 80, 504 rate down to 2.3%. Canary stable.
lyra-support: Customer reports improvement, most users recovered. They're keeping throttle in place for 45m.
sara: tagging this for follow-up postmortem and contract review — need formal burst clause for Lyra.
elaine: I'll document actions and collect logs/traces. Filing runbook: incident-2198765432.
mike: great job. I'll hand off to night on-call at 2198769000 UTC. Leave timeline + actions in the runbook.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to P2 at 2198766800. Spill scheduled until 2198767232.
(30m later) jia: Spill expired automatically; pool back on dedicated nodes. Metrics stable: GPU util 69%, 504s ~0.8%.
lyra-support: Customer says service is nominal. We'll keep reduced background jobs for 1h.
mike: closing alert, but keeping runbook open for postmortem. Action items: 1) add formal emergency-spill play in contract 2) enable canary promotion path for quantized variants 3) autoscaler config review for dedicated pools.
sara: ack on items, assign owners in runbook.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — 2198767232. Postmortem requested.
